title: Shading by stitch density
subtitle: More stitches per square centimetre reads darker; fewer reads lighter
excerpt: Blackwork creates the appearance of shade by varying how densely the fill pattern is stitched. A tight fill looks dark from a distance. An open fill looks light. No shading thread is needed: the pattern itself carries the tonal value.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Weldon's Practical Needlework (1880s), blackwork sampler chapters discussing fill density.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small repeating geometric unit worked inside an outline shape in blackwork. Different fill patterns have different visual densities.
How many stitches per unit area a fill pattern places on the cloth. High density reads dark; low density reads light.

content.text: within a single design. You choose one colour of thread throughout; the pattern arrangement creates the tonal effect.

Hold a blackwork fill sample at arm's length and half-close your eyes. The stitched sections merge into a mid-grey tone. A denser fill merges into darker grey. A sparser fill becomes light grey. This is the principle: the eye averages the black-and-white ratio across a small area and reads it as a single tone.
Ordering fills from light to dark
Work a sample of each fill you plan to use on a spare scrap of cloth. Use the same thread and fabric as the final piece.
Hold the samples at arm's length and rank them from lightest to darkest. Label each sample with its name so you can refer to the ranking when planning the design.
Plan which areas of the design should read darkest (areas in shadow or closest to the viewer in a portrait or botanical design) and which should read lightest.
Assign the ranked fills to the design areas, matching density to desired tone.

A hard edge between a dark fill and a light fill works well for graphic designs. For a softer transition, use a border fill at an intermediate density between the two. Three tones (light, medium, dark) are enough to create a convincing graduation across most pieces.
for a shaded piece, note that each fill area may carry a different chart, or the same chart may be marked with density zones. Check the chart key before starting.
